[IMG]

Product 'A' in the above chemical reaction is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\mathrm{CCl}{}_{4}$ without peroxide, $\mathrm{HBr}$ adds by the ionic route. Protonation of the terminal $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ of the vinyl group gives a secondary carbocation on the side-chain carbon attached to the quaternary ring carbon that carries the methyl group.

A 1,2-methyl shift from the ring carbon to this cationic carbon gives a tertiary carbocation on the ring carbon, which now bears an isopropyl group. Expansion to a cycloheptyl cation offers no strain relief over the strain-free cyclohexane ring and is not favoured.

Bromide adds to the tertiary carbocation, giving 1-bromo-1-isopropylcyclohexane.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Retardation factor $(R_{f})$ can be measured in meter/centimeter.

Statement II : $R_{f}$ value of a compound remains constant in all solvents.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is true but statement II is false
Statement I is false but statement II is true
Both statement I and statement II are true
Both statement I and statement II are false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Retardation factor $(R_{f})$ is the ratio of the distance
moved by the substance from the baseline to the
distance moved by the solvent from the baseline.
So, it is dimensionless. The distance moved by the
substance is due to the adsorption of the substance on
the stationary phase. It does not depend on the
nature of the solvent. But the distance moved by the
solvent will change with the nature of the solvent.
Therefore, $R_{f}$ will vary with the change in the solvent.

So, both the statements are false.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift

text:
The mole fraction of a solute in a 100 molal aqueous solution is $___________$ $\times$ $10^{-2}. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer).

[Given : Atomic masses : H : 1.0 u, O : 16.0 u ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let weight of $H_{2}O = 1000 g$

Moles of solute = 100

(mole$)H_{2}O =$ $\frac{1000}{18}$

Mole fraction of solute = $\frac{moleofsolute}{Totalmoles}$

$=\frac{100}{100+\frac{1000}{18}}=\frac{1800}{2800}$

$X_{solute}=64\times 10^{-2}$

text:
The oxygen dissolved in water exerts a partial pressure of 20 kPa in the vapour above water. The molar solubility of oxygen in water is $__________$ $\times$ $10^{-5}$ mol $dm^{-3}. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer).

[Given : Henry's law constant $= K_{H} = 8.0$ $\times$ $10^{4}$ kPa for $O_{2}$. Density of water with dissolved oxygen $= 1.0 kg dm^{-3}$ ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With $K_{H}$ in pressure units, Henry's law relates the partial pressure to the mole fraction of the gas: $p=K_{H}x$.

$x_{\mathrm{O}{}_{2}}=\dfrac{20}{8.0\times 10^{4}}=2.5\times 10^{-4}$

$1\text{dm}^{3}$ of the solution has a mass of $1.0\text{kg}$, practically all water, so $n_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}}=\dfrac{1000}{18}=55.56\text{mol}$.

Since $x$ is small, $n_{\mathrm{O}{}_{2}}\approx xn_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}}=2.5\times 10^{-4}\times 55.56=1.389\times 10^{-2}\text{mol}$.

Molar solubility $=1.389\times 10^{-2}\text{mol dm}^{-3}=1389\times 10^{-5}\text{mol dm}^{-3}$.

Hence, the answer is 1389.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift
